caveat: Faithful-core harness: the vulnerable SINK is the REAL published npm axios bytes (axios@1.7.3/1.7.4/1.8.2 installed side-by-side via npm aliases), exercised via a minimal Node destination-pinned proxy server (axios.get(userPath, baseURL public-app, allowAbsoluteUrls false)) rather than a full downstream application. Sink is genuine library code; the surrounding app is a thin harness.

audit.evidence: real node:20-slim build with real npm axios 1.7.3/1.7.4/1.8.2; external HTTP entry GET server?path=... baseURL destination-override SSRF to internal-sidecar. Observed: original protocol-relative //internal-sidecar reaches flag@v0, blocked@v1 (CVE-2024-39338 fix); residual fully-absolute http://internal-sidecar reaches flag@v1, blocked@v2 (allowAbsoluteUrls:false honored, CVE-2025-27152). relative path stays on public-app all versions. passed=true
audit.lift_correction: real published npm axios 1.7.3/1.7.4/1.8.2 bytes (not a reimplementation) wrapped in minimal HTTP service + external HTTP trigger = compliant per library-CVE policy

app_purpose: Node.js destination-pinned outbound HTTP client: app sets baseURL to the one allowed upstream and lets a user supply only the request path (webhook relay / image proxy / link-preview fetcher)
root_cause: SSRF via baseURL destination-control bypass in buildFullPath/isAbsoluteURL + http-adapter URL resolution (CWE-918)

v0.ref: npm axios@1.7.3 lib/adapters/http.js:232 `new URL(fullPath, 'http://localhost')` (protocol-relative //host inherits http scheme -> overrides baseURL)

v1.ref: npm axios@1.7.4 lib/adapters/http.js:232 `new URL(fullPath, utils.hasBrowserEnv ? platform.origin : undefined)` (CVE-2024-39338 fix: //host now throws; INCOMPLETE — a fully-absolute http://host URL still passes isAbsoluteURL and still overrides baseURL). buildFullPath.js/isAbsoluteURL.js byte-identical to 1.7.3.

v2.ref: npm axios@1.8.2 lib/core/buildFullPath.js 3-arg `buildFullPath(baseURL, requestedURL, allowAbsoluteUrls)` + Axios.js allowAbsoluteUrls default true (CVE-2025-27152 fix: allowAbsoluteUrls:false combineURLs even an absolute path -> destination stays pinned to baseURL)

flag.resource: internal-only sidecar service `internal-sidecar` (distinct hostname, listens :80, NO published host port) reachable only via a baseURL destination-override from the axios server
flag.placement: harness.mjs ROLE=sidecar serves ${PCB_FLAG} on any path inside its own container; baseURL is pinned to a different host (public-app), which serves a benign non-flag body
flag.detect: flag token substring in the candidate result body (server echoes the fetched upstream body)

evidence.fix_reference: npm axios@1.7.4 lib/adapters/http.js:232 `new URL(fullPath, utils.hasBrowserEnv ? platform.origin : undefined)` (CVE-2024-39338 fix: //host now throws; INCOMPLETE — a fully-absolute http://host URL still passes isAbsoluteURL and still overrides baseURL). buildFullPath.js/isAbsoluteURL.js byte-identical to 1.7.3.; npm axios@1.8.2 lib/core/buildFullPath.js 3-arg `buildFullPath(baseURL, requestedURL, allowAbsoluteUrls)` + Axios.js allowAbsoluteUrls default true (CVE-2025-27152 fix: allowAbsoluteUrls:false combineURLs even an absolute path -> destination stays pinned to baseURL)
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: A previously reported issue (protocol-relative URL SSRF) ... A similar problem that occurs when passing ABSOLUTE URLs ... Even if baseURL is set, axios sends the request to the specified absolute URL, [which] could lead to SSRF. This is an incomplete-fix follow-up to the protocol-relative fix (CVE-2024-39338).

provenance.notes: Faithful-core harness: the REAL npm `axios` package installed per-version via npm aliases (axios@1.7.3=V0, axios@1.7.4=V1, axios@1.8.2=V2). One image, three roles by ROLE env: public-app (baseURL host, benign body, :80), internal-sidecar (${PCB_FLAG}, :80, NO host port, distinct hostname), server (destination-pinned axios.get(userPath,{baseURL:'http://public-app',allowAbsoluteUrls:false})). App code byte-identical across profiles; only the axios version differs. Variant A gate passes; V2 negative control confirms the 1.8.2 complete fix; a plain relative path /data stays on public-app on all versions (baseURL not trivially bypassable). Gate via `PCB_FLAG=<tok> python3 oracle.py --wait`; see repro.log. No reject condition triggered.
